name: freetype
notes: Added 2026-08-24 as Phase 1 of the 'notepad-capability' plan: real text rendering needs a real font rasterizer, and Skia already has first-class, non-host support for FreeType (skia_use_freetype/SkFontMgr_custom_* GN targets exist upstream, just currently off -- see libcrtgfx's own build_skia.py, skia_enable_fontmgr_custom_empty=true/skia_use_freetype=false). Porting FreeType itself is the prerequisite before touching any Skia GN flags.

Version 2.14.3 (2026-03-22), the current stable release at recipe-creation time. The savannah.gnu.org mirror listed in the official download page redirected to an unreachable third-party mirror (ftp.cc.uoc.gr) when fetched directly; the identical tarball was fetched from the project's own SourceForge release instead (https://sourceforge.net/projects/freetype/files/freetype2/2.14.3/freetype-2.14.3.tar.xz/download) and source.sha256/sha1/md5 were computed directly from that real downloaded copy, matching this project's own SHA256-is-authoritative policy. tools/fetch_ports.py's own download() only ever uses source.url (savannah), not the SourceForge mirror used to obtain this recipe's own hashes -- if savannah's own redirect target is unreachable again when this recipe is actually fetched, that is a real, separate problem to solve then (retry, or point source.url at a working mirror), not something this recipe's own hash values need to change for.

The release tarball's own top-level ./configure is a thin wrapper (builds/unix/configure.raw's own convention) that forwards its arguments into `$MAKE setup unix`, which itself invokes the real, ~20000-line autotools-generated builds/unix/configure -- confirmed by reading configure directly, not assumed. On Linux/macOS this fits crt-port-build.py's existing 'configure' build system completely unmodified and was verified for real (2026-08-24, Linux x64/WSL): the wrapper reads $MAKE/$GNUMAKE from the environment exactly like every other step of this project's own configure-based recipes already does, and both automated tests (glyph-rasterize-static/-shared) passed against a real rendered 'A' glyph on the first real build attempt. On Windows the same recursive `$MAKE setup unix` call was found genuinely broken on this PAL (2026-08-24): the nested make.exe -- a real, non-mksh-aware native Windows GNU Make -- cannot resolve real toybox applets (cat/cp) through this project's own rootfs-relative $PATH on its own, and forcing it through mksh via SHELL= (the technique that already works for every *non-recursive* make invocation in tools/crt-port-build.py) instead produced a silent, hard crash (exit 139, no output at all) -- a real instability in nested mksh-launched-from-make process spawning on this PAL. Root-caused (by reading builds/toplevel.mk/builds/unix/detect.mk directly) that `$MAKE setup unix`, for an in-tree build, only ever does two real things: `cp builds/unix/unix.mk config.mk` and `cd builds/unix && ./configure $CFG` (the real autoconf script, one directory down) -- builds/toplevel.mk's own `ifeq ($(wildcard $(CONFIG_MK)),) ... else include $(CONFIG_MK)` check confirms pre-existing a real config.mk skips the whole recursive-make detection dance entirely. Windows now replicates those two steps directly via two new, generic tools/crt-port-build.py recipe fields (configure_cwd/pre_configure_copy, read from target_overrides.<os> the same way configure_args already is -- see this recipe's own windows target_overrides above) instead of the crashy recursive make -- no engine change was needed on Linux/macOS, which keep using upstream's own wrapper unmodified.

--with-zlib=no/--with-bzip2=no/--with-png=no/--with-harfbuzz=no/--with-brotli=no keep this first pass to FreeType's own core TrueType/OpenType outline parsing and rasterization only -- none of the disabled optional codecs (compressed PCF bitmap fonts, embedded PNG color bitmaps, HarfBuzz-assisted auto-hinting for certain complex scripts, WOFF2 decompression) are needed to render a plain TTF/OTF outline font, the actual target use case (DejaVuSansMono.ttf, see this recipe's own tests). zlib and bzip2 are both already-ported dependencies this project could wire in later if a real need for compressed bitmap fonts ever comes up; harfbuzz/brotli would each be real new ports of their own.

--disable-mmap is the one flag that actually matters for Windows portability, not just a minor optimization toggle: confirmed directly by reading builds/unix/configure.ac that a *-*-mingw* host (needed anyway for config.guess via --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@, the same workaround libpng.json/pcre2.json/xz.json/expat.json already use) selects FTSYS_SRC='$(TOP_DIR)/builds/windows/ftsystem.c' -- a real Win32 MapViewOfFile-based implementation this project's own freestanding sysroot has no real <windows.h> to satisfy (the same class of host-SDK-leakage problem zlib/libpng/pcre2/xz all hit and fixed with a CFLAGS -U_WIN32 trick instead, since their own leaks were inside FreeType's -- sorry, THEIR OWN -- unconditionally-compiled source, not a separate host-selected file the way FreeType's is). --disable-mmap skips that whole case statement, leaving FTSYS_SRC unset, which configure.ac's own fallback then resolves to src/base/ftsystem.c -- FreeType's own fully portable, plain stdio-based (fopen/fread/fseek) generic implementation, already well within this project's own proven libc surface. Applied unconditionally (not Windows-only) for one consistent code path across every target this project builds for, since mmap-vs-stdio is a minor I/O optimization for a font-loading library, not a functional requirement.

porting/tests/freetype_glyph_test.c is a real FT_New_Face()/FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes()/FT_Load_Char(..., FT_LOAD_RENDER) round trip against a real bundled font file (libcrtgfx/assets/fonts/DejaVuSansMono.ttf, see that directory's own README.md for provenance/license) -- FT_LOAD_RENDER rasterizes directly inside FT_Load_Char, no separate FT_Render_Glyph() call needed (confirmed via real freetype.h reading, not assumed) -- checking the resulting FT_Bitmap (face->glyph->bitmap) has plausible non-zero dimensions AND at least one genuinely non-zero (inked) byte in its buffer, not just that FreeType's own API calls returned success codes. -I@PORT_PREFIX@/include/freetype2 (not @PORT_PREFIX@/include directly): FreeType's own install layout nests its real public headers one directory deeper than most other ports in this queue, confirmed by reading builds/unix/freetype2.in's own installed pkg-config Cflags value.

Windows also hit a real, general stack-overflow bug in this project's own ported make.exe (2026-08-24, found and fixed building this recipe for real, see porting/recipes/make.json's own matching note): make.exe silently segfaults (no output at all) partway through reading freetype's own unusually large Makefile tree -- ld.lld's default 1 MiB PE stack reserve is enough for every other, much flatter configure-based recipe's Makefile in this queue, but not for FreeType's. Fixed generally in make.json itself (target_overrides.windows.env.LDFLAGS=-Wl,--stack,16777216, a 16 MiB reserve), not here -- this recipe needed no field of its own for that fix, just a rebuilt make.exe (`port-rebuild-make`) before rebuilding this recipe.

windows target_overrides.env.RC="" (empty, overriding the general Windows $RC=llvm-rc.exe convention every other Windows configure-based recipe in this queue relies on -- see e.g. xz.json's own liblzma_w32res.rc use of the same $RC): FreeType's own builds/freetype.mk has a hand-rolled `ifneq ($(RC),) ... $(FTVER_OBJ): $(FTVER_SRC) \n\t$(RC) -o $@ $<` rule (not an Automake-generated one) that, once routed through builds/unix/libtool's own --mode=compile wrapper (FreeType's unix.mk always compiles through libtool, even for non-C sources), reorders/mis-wraps the llvm-rc.exe invocation into an argv shape it rejects outright (`Exactly one input file should be provided`) -- confirmed via a real build attempt (2026-08-24). ftver.rc is purely a Windows DLL/EXE VERSIONINFO resource (copyright/version strings shown in Explorer's file Properties dialog), no functional effect on font rasterization at all, so forcing $(RC) empty (which FreeType's own `ifneq ($(RC),)` guard treats as 'no resource compiler available', matching real behavior on any host with no windres/rc.exe) skips the broken rule entirely rather than fixing libtool's own RC-wrapping logic -- a real, scoped workaround, not a functional regression for this port's own actual purpose (glyph rasterization, not embedding Windows version metadata).

--with-pic added 2026-08-24, found wiring Skia's real SkFontMgr_custom_directory in (libcrtgfx/CMakeLists.txt's own CRTGFX_SKIA_LIBRARIES, see that file's own notes): linking libcrtgfx.so (a real shared library, Linux) against the static libfreetype.a this recipe's own tests had only ever linked into a plain executable before failed outright -- `ld.lld: error: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 cannot be used against symbol 'TT_RunIns'; recompile with -fPIC`. Root cause is real and well understood, not this project's own PAL: GNU Libtool's own default behavior deliberately builds the static archive (.a) with non-PIC object code (a minor codegen optimization, correct and sufficient for every static-into-executable link, exactly what this recipe's own two automated tests already exercise) and only the shared object (.so/.dylib/.dll) with PIC code -- non-PIC code is fundamentally incompatible with linking into ANY shared object afterward, on any host, because PC-relative relocations assume a fixed load address a shared object's position-independent code model can't guarantee. `--with-pic` is libtool's own standard, documented flag (confirmed via a real `grep with_pic` on the generated configure script) forcing the static archive to ALSO build with -fPIC -- applied unconditionally (not Linux-only) for the same 'one consistent code path' reasoning already used for --disable-mmap above, since this project intends to link FreeType into shared libcrtgfx builds on every host eventually, not just Linux.

Verified for real end to end (2026-08-24), both hosts: Linux x64/WSL -- both glyph-rasterize-static and glyph-rasterize-shared passed on the first real build attempt, no bugs found (a real rendered 'A' glyph bitmap, non-zero dimensions and at least one inked pixel, confirmed by the test's own assertions, not just a successful compile). Windows x64 -- both tests also passed, after finding and fixing three real, general bugs along the way (all documented above and in their own general-fix locations, not narrowly patched around): the TOP_DIR drive-letter-colon GNU Make static-pattern-rule syntax collision (fixed via this recipe's own configure_cwd/pre_configure_copy/post_configure_patch target_overrides, two of those fields new and generic in tools/crt-port-build.py), this project's own ported make.exe silently stack-overflowing on FreeType's unusually large Makefile tree (fixed generally in porting/recipes/make.json's own Windows LDFLAGS, not here), and libtool mis-wrapping the Windows VERSIONINFO resource compiler for FreeType's own hand-rolled ftver.rc rule (worked around via this recipe's own windows target_overrides.env.RC="", a real but narrowly-scoped fix specific to a purely cosmetic resource this port's actual purpose does not need). Full regression check after all fixes: 100% (121/121) ctest on Windows, and Linux's own full rebuild plus every real (non-tty-dependent) test also passed with no regressions -- see HISTORY.md's 2026-08-24 entries for the complete trail. macOS not attempted this session.

dependencies added "make" (2026-08-25, first real macOS attempt, `crtgfx-skia-build`): this recipe's own build.system is "configure", and tools/crt-port-build.py's build_port() unconditionally builds+installs the `make` port before any configure-system recipe on every host (see porting/recipes/make.json's own notes) -- but that rule lives only in crt-port-build.py, not in tools/fetch_ports.py's dependency resolution, which instead walks each recipe's own declared `dependencies` array to decide what to fetch. Since this recipe's own dependencies was empty, CMake's per-port `port-fetch-freetype` target (crt_add_port_recipe_target(freetype), CMakeLists.txt) only ever fetched freetype's own archive, never make's -- confirmed for real: `port-build-freetype` failed with `source not found: .../port-tests/src/toolchain-make-...` the first time this recipe was ever built completely standalone (crtgfx-skia-build's own crt_add_build_port_target(freetype ...) call fetches only this one port, unlike crtgfx-wayland-smoke's port-tests tree, where libffi.json's own pre-existing `dependencies: ["make"]` had already pulled make's source into the same shared src/ directory as a side effect, masking the identical gap there). Fixed by declaring `make` as a real dependency here too, exactly matching libffi.json/zlib.json's own existing precedent for the same reason -- this only changes what tools/fetch_ports.py fetches, not anything about the build itself (crt-port-build.py already built make first regardless, dependencies or not). expat.json/mbedtls.json/pcre2.json/xz.json share the identical empty-dependencies gap and were fixed the same way in the same pass, once this class of bug was found and confirmed here. Once fixed, verified for real on macOS for the first time (status macos: pending -> shared-pass): `port-build-freetype` builds and installs cleanly against the crtgfx-skia-smoke tree, and both glyph-rasterize-static and glyph-rasterize-shared print `freetype_glyph_test: ok` (a real rendered DejaVuSansMono glyph, same assertions as the Linux/Windows runs above).
